# Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree). Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5. Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments. ## 1. Purpose Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn: - **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts). - **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed. - **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task. - **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check). - **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: ` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked. - **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID. - **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts. - **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated. Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`. ## 2. Entrypoints and control flow ### CLI dispatch (`internal/app/sprint_commands.go:329-368`) - Flag parsing `parseSprintExecuteArgs` (1193-1233): `--task `, `--dry-run|--prompt`, `--resume`, `--defer --reason `, `--model `. Constraints: `--defer` requires `--task`; `--defer` cannot combine with `--dry-run`, `--resume`, or `--model`. Unknown flags → ExitUsage. - Non-dry-run, non-defer runs are wrapped as durable operations: `beginDurableCLICommand(OperationExecuteStart, ...Task: req.TaskID)` (durable_operations.go:49-138 — run-control acceptance, owner claim with lease+fencing, running lifecycle event, heartbeat/cancel-watch goroutine). The command context becomes cancellation-aware. Service is rebuilt via `sprintRuntimeService` (685-711) with the real runtime, publisher (`stagePublisher`: nil publisher when `git.stage_completion=off`), stage runtime models, QA/smoke settings. - Deferral runs `DeferExecuteTask` on the plain (non-runtime) service against `deps.ctx`; no durable wrapper. - Error classification after render: findings present → ExitValidation; error contains "failed tasks" → ExitPartial; contains "runtime" → ExitRuntime; otherwise `mapSprintError`. - Output rendering `renderSprintExecute` (1372-1402): project/sprint, dry-run prompt dump, result message, run-state/summary paths, per-task `id status attempts=N` lines, findings list. Help text at 1530-1531, 1571-1580. ### Web / TUI / flow entrypoints - Web operation spec `"execute"|"execute-start"` maps to `OperationExecuteStatus | OperationExecuteDryRun | OperationExecuteResume | OperationExecuteStart` based on options (`internal/web/operation_handlers.go:646-666`). TUI exposes Execute Status/Dry Run/Start/Resume nav items (`internal/tui/model.go:480-483`). - `internal/app/operation_runner.go:53-58`: execute-start/resume → `service.Execute(ctx, p, s, ExecuteRequest{TaskID, ModelOverride, Resume: kind==OperationExecuteResume})`; dry-run variant at `operations.go:443`. - Flow integration (`internal/sprint/flow.go`): execute is the 8th cumulative stage; `runFlowStage` case StageExecute → `s.Execute(ctx, ..., ExecuteRequest{DryRun: req.DryRun, Resume: true})` (flow.go:241) — flow always resumes. Flow skips its generic planning-stage publication for execute (execute publishes itself, flow.go:142-155, 167) and uses `ExecuteComplete` for the skip check (flow.go:307-308 → verify.go:134-140). ### `Service.Execute` main loop (`internal/sprint/execute.go:129-349`) 1. Acquire mutation lock unless DryRun (`acquireMutationContext`, locks.go:112-126 — cross-process file lease shared by flow/execute/review/smoke/verify; reentrant via context marker). 2. `prepareExecute` (351-384): resolve sprint inputs → `planManifest` → `resolveSprintTarget(create=false)` → read plan artifact → `extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, allowChecked=req.Resume)` → if Resume, `validateResolvedResumeTasks` → TaskID existence check → `executeModelSelection(override)` (override > planning.execute_model > planning.plan_model > runtime provider/model; unresolved model ⇒ finding). Any finding aborts before any write ("execute prerequisites failed validation"). 3. Read planning inputs; `prepareSharedPromptContext(..., persistCache=true)` — code-context-derived shared prefix, cached context pack, fails closed when code-context exists but is invalid (`prompt_context.go:93-123`). 4. DryRun: composes the first (or selected) task's prompt and returns; no state writes, no runtime. 5. Fresh vs resumed state: `records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, now)`; `state := NewExecuteRunState(sp, target, planPath, PlanFingerprint(mustReadPlan), records, now)`. If `req.Resume` AND load succeeds → `state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)` (existing records substituted by ID into planned order; stale `running` → `failed` with "recovered stale running task on resume"). Load errors on resume are ignored (fresh state wins). Then unconditional `SaveExecuteRunState`. 6. `executionQueue := executeQueueFromState(state.Tasks, tasks, req.TaskID)` — planned tasks whose record is not complete/deferred, optionally narrowed to one ID. 7. Session reuse gate (186-193): only when `req.Resume` and `state.Target.Path == target.Path`; picks the last filtered record whose Runtime.Model equals the first queued task's effective model and has a SessionID (`reusableExecuteSession`, 563-574). 8. Per-task loop over `state.Tasks` (skips others when TaskID set): - Skip `complete`; `running` → `failed` + "stale-running ... before resume" diagnostic; proceed only if now pending|failed|cancelled. - Mark running, `Attempts++`, StartedAt; persist — failure aborts before launch ("persist running execute task %q"). - Per-task model: inline plan annotation `` overrides batch selection (`executeSelectionForTask`, 739-744). - `continueSession := batchSessionID != "" && models match` → compact `RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt` with empty prefix and `SessionAction="continue"`; otherwise full `renderExecuteSessionPrompt` (RenderExecutePrompt + ordered queue section + direct-input packet: project definition inputs, sprint-index, technical-handbook, reasoning directory inputs, reasoning.md, plan.md). - Metadata: session_mode initial|continue|fresh-fallback, execution_turn, execution_queue_size, model_source, stage, task. - `runtimeRequest` (service.go:1122-1169): scoped runtime store owner/path under the sprint dir, PromptRef with sha256 checksum, trace ID, stable-prefix cache directive. `runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path` (execute.go:245). `OnEvent` wrapper checkpoints any new SessionID into run state under a mutex (save errors captured, surfaced post-run). - `startSprintRuntime` (runtime_metrics.go:116-125): `pruntime.CleanupRuntimeStores(sp.Path, 72h, 2GiB, false)` then `runtime.StartRun`; runtime metrics persisted separately (failure degrades to warning). - Post-run classification precedence (287-313): checkpoint save error → failed/"state-save-failed"; deferral read-back error → failed/"invalid-deferral"; deferral reason non-empty → deferred + rationale diagnostic; ctx cancelled → cancelled; runtime error → failed/"runtime-failed"; ≥1 artifact → complete + evidence entries (paths sanitized by `safeArtifactPath`); warning containing "diagnostic-only" → complete + "diagnostic-only-completion"; else failed/"missing-evidence". - Terminal state persisted ("persist terminal execute task"); checkpoint errors abort the whole command afterwards. Failed or cancelled breaks the loop; single-task mode always breaks. - On success, batchSessionID/batchSessionModel advance from the run result (or task.Runtime fallback). 9. `WriteExecuteSummary` → `projects/

/sprints//execute.md` (plain `os.WriteFile` 0644 inside contained path): counts per status, per-task attempts/evidence/diagnostics lines. 10. Any failed/cancelled ⇒ returns result plus error "execute completed with failed tasks". 11. Best-effort `_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(...)` per runtime result (deletes session(s)/runtime store; flow.go:26-56). 12. If `allExecuteTasksResolved` (≥1 task, all complete|deferred) → `publishExecuteStage` (publication.go:57-78): implementation publish `{Root: target.Path, All: true}` then workspace publish of `execute.md` + `.run-state.json`; identical commit message "ultraplan: sprint

/ complete execute" with `UltraPlan-Publication:` identity trailer; skipped results filtered when publisher disabled. ### `DeferExecuteTask` (execute.go:29-79) Trims reason; requires non-empty taskID+reason, ≤1000 chars, no `\x00\r\n`. Mutation lock; loads state; rejects deferring complete/deferred tasks; marks deferred (+CompletedAt, "deferred" diagnostic with redacted reason); saves state and summary; unknown ID errors. Does not modify plan.md. ### Resume validation (`validateResolvedResumeTasks`, execute.go:386-421) When resuming and plan.md has `[x]` or `[/]` top-level markers: requires a loadable valid run state ("checked tasks lack execution state" otherwise); each resolved marker must map to matching status (`[x]`→complete, `[/]`→deferred) by task ID; mismatches become blocking findings. ### Target resolution (`ResolveExecuteTarget` / `resolveSprintTarget`, execute_target.go) - Extract `**Target Implementation Directory:**` (bold or plain bullet, backtick-trimmed) from project-index.md; absolute or workspace-root-relative; must stat to an existing directory. - If `.workspace.json` exists it wins (Source ".workspace.json"): validated against current source root (clean-path equality), worktree dir exists and is a dir, same git common dir as source, current branch equals recorded branch. Invalid → findings; unreadable/malformed → findings; absent + create=false → raw source target. - Worktree creation happens at the code-context stage (`create=true` in flow.go:138), not here: `createSprintWorkspace` requires the source be a clean git worktree root (no uncommitted changes), creates `ultraplan//` branch at HEAD under sibling `.basename-ultraplan-worktrees/` dir, writes `.workspace.json` atomically (rollback removes worktree+branch if the record write fails). ### Publication mechanics (`internal/platform/gitpublish/publisher.go`) Modes off|commit|commit-and-push. Resolves repo root + current branch (detached HEAD rejected), acquires `ultraplan-publish.lock` in the git common dir, builds a temporary index (`read-tree parent`, `add -A -- paths`, `write-tree`), skips commit when tree equals parent tree, else `commit-tree -p parent` + `update-ref commit parent` (CAS against concurrent branch movement) + index reconcile. Push honors upstream remote/ref, else pushes HEAD to configured remote with `--set-upstream`; `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, push timeout (default 2m). Path requests are containment-checked against the repo root. ## 3. Inputs / outputs Inputs: - argv flags; workspace root; cwd/env via workspace discovery. - `project-index.md` `Project Scope > Target Implementation Directory` line (agent-writable planning artifact; selects both the agent workdir and the wholesale-commit root). - `plan.md` content: top-level `- [ ] Task N: Name` checkboxes (bold-tolerant), nested `- [ ]` steps, `>` quote lines scanned for `Decision N` / `REQ-N-N` / `AC-N` refs, evidence heuristics (step text containing evidence/verification/test/check), `- [/]` deferral markers with `— Deferred:`/`- Deferred:` suffix reasons, inline `` annotations. Plan must pass `ValidatePlanContent` against the plan manifest first. - Planning inputs packet (requirements/code-context/sprint-index/handbook/reasoning dirs/reasoning.md/plan.md) rendered into the first-turn prompt. - `.run-state.json` or productstate DB record (schemaVersion 1) for resume/status; legacy schemaVersion-0 terminal files recognized read-only. - `.workspace.json` worktree record; config keys (`planning.execute_model`, `planning.plan_model`, `models.primary/default`, `git.stage_completion|remote|push_timeout`, runtime config); live agent runtime. Outputs: - Human stdout render; exit codes (0 ok / 2 usage / validation-class / partial for failed tasks / runtime-class). - Files written: `.run-state.json` (atomic temp+fsync+rename+dir-sync, JSON indent+newline), `execute.md` (plain truncate-write), runtime metrics file, disposable context-pack cache. - Git commits and optional pushes in two repos (implementation worktree, workspace) when all tasks resolved and publishing enabled. - Durable run-control events (accept/claim/lifecycle/heartbeat/terminal) for non-dry-run CLI executions. - Runtime side effects delegated to the agent: file edits inside WorkDir=target.Path, test execution, etc. ## 4. Authoritative state - **`.run-state.json` schemaVersion 1** (`domain.go:12,122-133`): header {schemaVersion, project, sprint, target{path,source}, planPath (contained relative), planFingerprint `sha256:` of whitespace-normalized lowercase plan text, createdAt, updatedAt} + ordered `tasks[]` {id `task-<12 hex>`, identity{name, planLine≥1, decisions[], requirements[], evidence[]}, status, attempts≥0, createdAt, updatedAt, startedAt?, completedAt?, diagnostics[], evidence[], runtime?}. - Statuses: pending / running / complete / deferred / failed / cancelled; terminal = complete|deferred|failed|cancelled (`domain.go:63-70`, execute_state.go:271-273). - **Validation contract** `ValidateExecuteRunState` (execute_state.go:184-268): strict schemaVersion==1; project/sprint identity match; safe contained planPath; fingerprint charset (no `\x00\r\n`); ≥1 task; unique IDs; safe identity text; deferred requires completedAt + a `deferred` diagnostic with non-blank rationale; running requires startedAt; terminal requires completedAt; diagnostics need code+message+time and safe charset; evidence needs kind+summary and optionally a safe relative path. - **Dual-home behavior**: when the productstate DB is enabled, the DB record is authoritative — `Save` writes DB first, then mirrors the file only once every task is terminal (checkpoint semantics, execute_state.go:105-130); `Load` prefers the DB record (state_database.go:38-55). Otherwise the file is primary. Migration hooks exist (`MigrateExecuteStateToDatabase`). - **Legacy compatibility**: schemaVersion-0 `{status: complete|failed|cancelled, files[], testsRun[], blockers[]}` files are historical evidence only (`LegacyTerminalExecuteStatus`), never resumable; `requireCompleteExecute` (verify.go:100-132) additionally accepts that legacy shape (status complete/completed with files[] plus non-empty execute.md) as completion evidence. - **`.workspace.json`** (`execute_target.go:16-27`): {schemaVersion:1, sourceRoot, path, branch, baseline, createdAt}; created at code-context stage; validated on every execute target resolution. - **`execute.md`**: derived human summary; plain WriteFile (not atomic); regenerated after every run/deferral. - **`plan.md`**: user-owned input; execute never writes it. The *agent* may edit markers during a turn; execute re-reads it after each turn (`agentDeferredTaskReason`, 423-450: full manifest + extraction revalidation, returning the marker reason only for the exact task). The recorded `PlanFingerprint` is captured once at state creation (via `mustReadPlan`, which swallows read errors) and is not re-verified later in the loop. - Note (descriptive): a resume attempt with unchecked plan tasks but an unreadable/malformed `.run-state.json` passes prepareExecute (no resolved markers ⇒ no findings; load error ignored at execute.go:177) and proceeds with fresh state, overwriting the prior file on first save. ## 5. Invariants (as implemented) - No runtime launch before the `running` transition is durably saved; no queue advance before the terminal outcome is saved; mid-stream session-ID events are also checkpointed. - Queue stops at the first failed or cancelled task; completed/deferred tasks are never re-executed within a run. - Resume reconciliation matches strictly by deterministic ID (normalized name+decisions+requirements+evidence hash); renamed/edited tasks get new IDs and their old records drop out of the reconciled list; deferral markers and model annotations deliberately do not change IDs (test-asserted). - Stale-running recovery exists in three layers: `ReconcileInterruptedMutation` (startup, code "recovery-interrupted"), `reconcileExecuteState` (resume), and the in-loop pre-execution check ("before resume"). - Deferral requires rationale at every layer: CLI flag validation, plan-marker regex requiring a reason, state-validation rationale diagnostic, and `invalid-deferral` classification when the read-back fails. - Completion gating: success requires ≥1 runtime artifact or an explicit "diagnostic-only" warning; otherwise failed/"missing-evidence". - Agent workdir is exactly the resolved target path (worktree preferred when valid); evidence paths stored in state must be safe relative paths or dropped. - Publication happens only when all tasks are terminal-resolved (complete|deferred); implementation repo commits before workspace artifacts; both silently skipped when publishing is off. - All persisted messages/diagnostics route through redaction/truncation helpers (`safeExecuteText` → `config.RedactValue`, ≤180 chars via `safeError`). - Session reuse additionally requires unchanged target path and equal effective model; otherwise fresh full prompts ("fresh-fallback"). ## 6. Trust boundaries - **plan.md as control input**: checkbox syntax, task names, decision/requirement references, deferral reasons, and `` annotations are parsed from an agent-writable artifact. The annotation string flows into runtime model selection without charset restriction beyond the annotation regex `[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]+`; marker deferral reasons are captured by regex without length limits at parse time (charset-checked later at state validation; redacted at persistence). - **project-index.md** decides which directory the agent may mutate and which repository gets committed wholesale (`All=true`) at publication. - **Agent output → durable state**: artifacts/warnings/session IDs from the runtime become state records; evidence URI must pass `safeRelPath` else stored empty; all free-text redacted. - **Agent constraints are prompt-level** (`ExecuteSafetyInstructions`, execute_target.go:220-227): stay inside approved target; do not create smoke/review/issues artifacts; do not run/request git mutation; no cross-sprint/TUI/hosted work. Technical enforcement of sandbox/permissions belongs to the opencode-agent-runtime surface (configured sandbox/permission policy travels on the runtime request). - **gitpublish** executes git with sanitized env (`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, LC_ALL=C), validates remote names (no leading dash, restricted charset), and CAS-updates the branch ref. - **Mutation serialization**: cross-process sprint mutation lease (file lock) plus durable run-control owner fencing serialize execute against flow/review/smoke/verify and other owners. ## 7. External effects & lifecycle semantics - Mutates the implementation repo (through the delegated agent), can commit and push it, commits workspace artifacts, deletes completed sessions/runtime stores best-effort, prunes stale runtime stores (>72h, >2GiB). - **Cancellation**: durable-context cancel during a turn classifies the task cancelled (+diagnostic), breaks the queue, persists, returns result with error; run-control finish records cancelled. The in-flight runtime call receives the same ctx. - **Crash/restart**: orphaned `running` records recover to failed on startup reconcile or next resume; cleanup-uncertain marker forces explicit operator handling instead of silent reconcile (locks.go:40-44,101-108); legacy terminal states remain readable. - **Retry**: rerunning without `--resume` rebuilds fresh state (prior file replaced on first save); failed/cancelled/pending tasks restart with Attempts++; `--resume` keeps complete/deferred history and continues the remaining queue, reusing the session when target and model still match. - **Partial failure**: mixed-status state persisted, execute.md reflects counts, command exits ExitPartial-class with "execute completed with failed tasks". - Publication failure after full resolution surfaces as command error while leaving all tasks resolved and state saved (commit may exist without push; push timeout bounded). ## 8. Immediate surface dependencies - **sprint-planning-chain**: `resolveSprintInputs`, `planManifest`, `ValidatePlanContent`, plan artifact reads, direct-input packet composition, shared prompt prefix/context pack. - **sprint-flow-state**: flow dispatches execute (always Resume:true), skips its own publish step for execute, gates skip-checks via `ExecuteComplete`; execute itself does not write flow-state.json. - **opencode-agent-runtime** (`internal/platform/runtime`): Request/Result/Event contract — SessionID/SessionAction continuation, OnEvent stream, Artifacts/Warnings driving completion classification, RuntimeStore scoping/cleanup, usage/metrics summaries. - **repo-publication** (`internal/platform/gitpublish`): policy modes, repo lock, temp-index commit strategy, push semantics. - **product-state-mirror** (`internal/productstate`): authoritative DB record {header, items keyed by task ID with ordinals} behind `ExecuteStateInDatabase`. - **run-control / durable operations**: acceptance, claim, fencing, heartbeats, cancellation watch, terminal proposals wrapping every non-dry-run CLI execute. - **workspace scaffold**: embedded `prompts/execute-sprint.md` documents the superseded agent-authored execution mode (writes legacy schemaVersion-0-style `.run-state.json` itself); still materialisable via `defaults install`. ## 9. Contracts (CURRENT-CONTRACT evidence) From target-repo `docs/cli-reference.md` (~L306-330, execute section): - One reusable agent session; first turn carries shared context + ordered queue; later tasks are compact continuations; UltraPlan checkpoints each task before advancing; stops on failure/cancellation; writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`; requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic before marking complete; constrains work to the project-index target; falls back to complete independent prompts when no reusable session ID is supplied. - Deferral: `--task --defer --reason ""` is durable and terminal, shown in execute.md and status counts; plan checkbox remains unchecked; review accepts deferrals only with a matching governed deferred outcome; arbitrary unchecked/manually checked tasks cannot bypass execution; `[/]` marker without `— Deferred: ` is invalid. From ultraplan-workspace sprint 23 (`projects/ultraplan-go/sprints/23-execute-stage/requirements.md` ~L22-49, L104): - Versioned, atomic, strictly-loaded, resumable `.run-state.json` recording statuses with attempts, timestamps, diagnostics, runtime metadata summaries; stale running tasks recovered to retryable-or-failed with diagnostics without redoing complete tasks; sprint status reflects execute readiness without runtime calls; execute.md cites plan.md and records counts/evidence/diagnostics; same-directory atomic writes; malformed/unsupported schemas rejected with actionable diagnostics. - Neutral divergence fact: sprint-23 enumerates five statuses (pending/running/complete/failed/cancelled); the implementation adds `deferred` as a sixth, documented instead in cli-reference.md. From ultraplan-workspace PRD (~L223, L576, L605): controlled execution from validated plan.md tasks is in scope; automatic Git-mutation *commands* and issue tracking remain deferred product non-goals (config-gated publication of completed work is implemented separately from the agent-side git ban). # Context Pack: `sprint-execute-resume` — Sprint execute queue and resume

Target: ultraplan-go @ 8eef70f4903b25580719960009a170945bdad9ad (frozen, clean tree).
Planning context: ultraplan-workspace @ ab12dc38059c9bf485f9aced9075bcd7d924cac5.
Domain: governed-sprint-delivery. Risk: high. Descriptive only — no defect judgments.

## 1. Purpose

Executes the top-level task checkboxes of a validated `plan.md` through a reusable agent session, with product-owned durability around every agent turn:

- **Queue execution**: one ordered pass over plan tasks; first turn gets shared sprint context + full queue; later turns are compact continuations in the same session when a reusable session ID exists (fallback: independent full prompts).
- **Persist-before-launch checkpointing**: each task is persisted as `running` before the runtime call, and its terminal outcome is persisted before the next task starts; session IDs observed mid-stream are also checkpointed.
- **Stop-on-failure discipline**: queue halts on the first failed or cancelled task.
- **Stale-running reconcile**: `running` records left by dead owners become `failed` with diagnostics at three distinct points (startup recovery, resume reconciliation, pre-execution check).
- **Deferral protocol**: CLI `--defer --reason` (operator) or an agent-authored plan marker `- [/] Task N: ... — Deferred: <reason>` (agent); both require rationale and produce durable `deferred` outcomes; the plan checkbox stays visibly unchecked.
- **Resume validation**: `--resume` allows checked/deferred plan markers only when the run state already records matching terminal outcomes per stable task ID.
- **Containment**: the agent's working directory is set to the resolved approved target (worktree preferred), with in-prompt safety constraints forbidding git mutation and out-of-scope artifacts.
- **Publication**: when every task resolves (complete|deferred), git publication commits the implementation worktree (`All=true`) then the workspace artifacts (`execute.md`, `.run-state.json`), config-gated.

Primary code: `internal/sprint/execute.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_state.go`, `execute_target.go`, `execute_model.go`, plus `internal/sprint/publication.go:57-78` and `internal/app/git_publication.go`.

150: 	sharedPrefix, err := s.prepareSharedPromptContext(ctx, sp, inputs, true)
151: 	if err != nil {
152: 		return result, err
153: 	}
154: 	if req.DryRun {
155: 		promptTask := tasks[0]
156: 		if req.TaskID != "" {
157: 			for _, task := range tasks {
158: 				if task.ID == req.TaskID {
159: 					promptTask = task
160: 					break
161: 				}
162: 			}
163: 		}
164: 		result.Prompt, err = composeStagePromptChecked(sharedPrefix, s.renderExecuteSessionPrompt(sp, promptTask, filterExecuteQueue(tasks, req.TaskID), target, executeSelectionForTask(selection, promptTask)))
165: 		if err != nil {
166: 			return result, err
167: 		}
168: 		result.Message = "execute dry run"
169: 		return result, nil
170: 	}
171: 	if s.runtime == nil {
172: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("runtime is required for execute")
173: 	}
174: 	now := s.now().UTC()
175: 	records := ExecuteTasksToRecords(tasks, func() time.Time { return now })
176: 	state := NewExecuteRunState(sp, target, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), PlanFingerprint(mustReadPlan(s, sp)), records, now)
177: 	if existing, loadErr := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp); loadErr == nil && req.Resume {
178: 		state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)
179: 	}
180: 	if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
181: 		return result, err
182: 	}
183: 	executionQueue := executeQueueFromState(state.Tasks, tasks, req.TaskID)
184: 	batchSessionID := ""
185: 	batchSessionModel := selection.Model
186: 	if req.Resume && filepath.Clean(state.Target.Path) == filepath.Clean(target.Path) {
187: 		if len(executionQueue) > 0 {
188: 			if first := taskByID(tasks, executionQueue[0].ID); first.ID != "" {
189: 				batchSessionModel = executeSelectionForTask(selection, first).Model
190: 			}
191: 		}
192: 		batchSessionID = reusableExecuteSession(state.Tasks, req.TaskID, batchSessionModel)
193: 	}
194: 	executionTurn := 0
195: 	for i := range state.Tasks {
196: 		task := &state.Tasks[i]
197: 		if req.TaskID != "" && task.ID != req.TaskID {
198: 			continue
199: 		}
200: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskComplete {
201: 			continue
202: 		}
203: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskRunning {
204: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
205: 			task.CompletedAt = ptrTime(now)
206: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "stale-running", Message: "recovered stale running task before resume", At: now})
207: 		}
208: 		if task.Status != ExecuteTaskPending && task.Status != ExecuteTaskFailed && task.Status != ExecuteTaskCancelled {
209: 			continue
210: 		}
211: 		start := s.now().UTC()
212: 		task.Status = ExecuteTaskRunning
213: 		task.Attempts++
214: 		task.StartedAt = &start
215: 		task.UpdatedAt = start
216: 		if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
217: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist running execute task %q: %w", task.ID, err)
218: 		}
219: 		planTask := taskByID(tasks, task.ID)
220: 		taskSelection := executeSelectionForTask(selection, planTask)
221: 		executionTurn++
222: 		continueSession := batchSessionID != "" && batchSessionModel == taskSelection.Model
223: 		stagePrompt := ""
224: 		promptPrefix := sharedPrefix
225: 		if continueSession {
226: 			stagePrompt = RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt(sp, planTask)
227: 			promptPrefix = ""
228: 		} else {
229: 			stagePrompt = s.renderExecuteSessionPrompt(sp, planTask, executionQueue, target, taskSelection)
230: 		}
231: 		composedPrompt, composeErr := composeStagePromptChecked(promptPrefix, stagePrompt)
232: 		if composeErr != nil {
233: 			return result, composeErr
234: 		}
235: 		sessionMode := "initial"
236: 		if continueSession {
237: 			sessionMode = "continue"
238: 		} else if executionTurn > 1 {
239: 			sessionMode = "fresh-fallback"
240: 		}
241: 		runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(composedPrompt, map[string]string{
242: 			"project": sp.Project, "sprint": sp.Slug, "stage": string(StageExecute), "task": task.ID, "model_source": taskSelection.Source,
243: 			"execution_session_mode": sessionMode, "execution_turn": fmt.Sprintf("%d", executionTurn), "execution_queue_size": fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(executionQueue)),
244: 		})
245: 		runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path
246: 		if continueSession {
247: 			runtimeReq.SessionID = batchSessionID
248: 			runtimeReq.SessionAction = "continue"
249: 		}
250: 		previousOnEvent := runtimeReq.OnEvent
251: 		var sessionMu sync.Mutex
252: 		var sessionSaveErr error
253: 		runtimeReq.OnEvent = func(event pruntime.Event) {
254: 			if previousOnEvent != nil {
255: 				previousOnEvent(event)
256: 			}
257: 			sessionMu.Lock()
258: 			defer sessionMu.Unlock()
259: 			if event.SessionID == "" || (task.Runtime != nil && task.Runtime.SessionID == event.SessionID) {
260: 				return
261: 			}
262: 			task.Runtime = &ExecuteRuntimeSummary{SessionID: event.SessionID, Model: taskSelection.Model, ModelSource: taskSelection.Source, OmissionReason: "raw runtime payloads omitted"}
263: 			task.UpdatedAt = s.now().UTC()
264: 			state.UpdatedAt = task.UpdatedAt
265: 			if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil && sessionSaveErr == nil {
266: 				sessionSaveErr = err
267: 			}
268: 		}
269: 		run, runErr := s.startSprintRuntime(ctx, sp, StageExecute, runtimeReq)
270: 		sessionMu.Lock()
271: 		checkpointErr := sessionSaveErr
272: 		sessionMu.Unlock()
273: 		result.Runtime = append(result.Runtime, run)
274: 		finish := s.now().UTC()
275: 		task.Runtime = mergeRuntimeSummary(task.Runtime, runtimeSummary(run, taskSelection))
276: 		if runErr == nil {
277: 			batchSessionID = run.SessionID
278: 			batchSessionModel = taskSelection.Model
279: 			if batchSessionID == "" && task.Runtime != nil {
280: 				batchSessionID = task.Runtime.SessionID
281: 			}
282: 		}
283: 		task.UpdatedAt = finish
284: 		task.CompletedAt = &finish
285: 		deferReason, deferErr := s.agentDeferredTaskReason(sp, task.ID)
286: 		switch {
287: 		case checkpointErr != nil:
288: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
289: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "state-save-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.state_save_error", checkpointErr.Error()), At: finish})
290: 		case deferErr != nil:
291: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
292: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "invalid-deferral", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_error", deferErr.Error()), At: finish})
293: 		case deferReason != "":
294: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskDeferred
295: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "deferred", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.defer_reason", deferReason), At: finish})
296: 		case ctx.Err() != nil:
297: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskCancelled
298: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.cancelled", ctx.Err().Error()), At: finish})
299: 		case runErr != nil:
300: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
301: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "runtime-failed", Message: safeExecuteText("execute.runtime_error", safeError(runErr)), At: finish})
302: 		case len(run.Artifacts) > 0:
303: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
304: 			for _, artifact := range run.Artifacts {
305: 				task.Evidence = append(task.Evidence, ExecuteEvidence{Kind: artifact.Kind, Summary: safeExecuteText("execute.evidence", firstNonEmptyString(artifact.Description, artifact.ID)), Path: safeArtifactPath(artifact.URI)})
306: 			}
307: 		case hasDiagnosticOnlyCompletion(run):
308: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskComplete
309: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "diagnostic-only-completion", Message: "runtime reported safe diagnostic-only completion", At: finish})
310: 		default:
311: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
312: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "missing-evidence", Message: "runtime succeeded without expected evidence", At: finish})
313: 		}
314: 		if err := SaveExecuteRunState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
315: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal execute task %q: %w", task.ID, err)
316: 		}
317: 		if checkpointErr != nil {
318: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("persist runtime session for execute task %q: %w", task.ID, checkpointErr)
319: 		}
320: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskFailed || task.Status == ExecuteTaskCancelled {
321: 			break
322: 		}
323: 		if req.TaskID != "" {
324: 			break
325: 		}
326: 	}
327: 	if err := WriteExecuteSummary(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
328: 		return result, err
329: 	}
330: 	statePath, _ := ExecuteRunStatePath(s.root, sp)
331: 	result.RunStatePath = workspace.Rel(s.root, statePath)
332: 	result.SummaryPath = ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute)
333: 	result.Tasks = state.Tasks
334: 	result.Message = executeResultMessage(state.Tasks)
335: 	if hasFailedExecuteTask(state.Tasks) {
336: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("execute completed with failed tasks")
337: 	}
338: 	for _, run := range result.Runtime {
339: 		_ = s.deleteCompletedSessions(ctx, run)
340: 	}
341: 	if allExecuteTasksResolved(state.Tasks) {
342: 		publications, publishErr := s.publishExecuteStage(ctx, sp, target)
343: 		result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
344: 		if publishErr != nil {
345: 			return result, publishErr
346: 		}
347: 	}
348: 	return result, nil
349: }

351: func (s Service) prepareExecute(projectRef, sprintRef string, req ExecuteRequest) (Sprint, []ExecutePlanTask, ExecuteTargetRef, ExecuteModelSelection, []ValidationFinding, error) {
352: 	sp, inputs, catalog, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
353: 	if err != nil {
354: 		return Sprint{}, nil, ExecuteTargetRef{}, ExecuteModelSelection{}, nil, err
355: 	}
356: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
357: 	var target ExecuteTargetRef
358: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
359: 		var targetFindings []ValidationFinding
360: 		target, targetFindings = s.resolveSprintTarget(sp, inputs.ProjectIndex, false)
361: 		findings = append(findings, targetFindings...)
362: 	}
363: 	var tasks []ExecutePlanTask
364: 	if len(findings) == 0 {
365: 		data, readErr := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
366: 		if readErr != nil {
367: 			findings = append(findings, finding("plan.md", "", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "missing plan", readErr.Error(), "Generate and validate plan.md before execute."))
368: 		} else {
369: 			tasks, findings = extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, req.Resume)
370: 			if req.Resume && len(findings) == 0 {
371: 				findings = append(findings, s.validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp, tasks, manifest.OutputPath)...)
372: 			}
373: 		}
374: 	}
375: 	if req.TaskID != "" && len(findings) == 0 && taskByID(tasks, req.TaskID).ID == "" {
376: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", req.TaskID, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "unknown execute task", "selected task id does not exist in plan.md", "Use a task id from validate execute or run without --task."))
377: 	}
378: 	selection := s.executeModelSelection(req.ModelOverride)
379: 	if selection.Model == "" {
380: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Configuration", "execute model", "", "missing execute model", "no execute model configured", "Set planning.execute_model, planning.plan_model, models.primary, or models.default."))
381: 	}
382: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
383: 	return sp, tasks, target, selection, findings, nil
384: }

386: func (s Service) validateResolvedResumeTasks(sp Sprint, tasks []ExecutePlanTask, planPath string) []ValidationFinding {
387: 	var resolved []ExecutePlanTask
388: 	for _, task := range tasks {
389: 		if task.Checked || task.Deferred {
390: 			resolved = append(resolved, task)
391: 		}
392: 	}
393: 	if len(resolved) == 0 {
394: 		return nil
395: 	}
396: 	state, err := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp)
397: 	if err != nil {
398: 		return []ValidationFinding{finding("Tasks", "", planPath, "checked tasks lack execution state", "one or more top-level tasks are checked but no valid resumable execution state exists", "Restore the matching .run-state.json or leave tasks unchecked for a new execution.")}
399: 	}
400: 	byID := make(map[string]ExecuteTaskStatus, len(state.Tasks))
401: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
402: 		byID[task.ID] = task.Status
403: 	}
404: 	var findings []ValidationFinding
405: 	for _, task := range resolved {
406: 		expected := ExecuteTaskComplete
407: 		problem := "checked task is not complete in execution state"
408: 		detail := "top-level task is checked without a matching complete run-state record"
409: 		suggestion := "Restore the task checkbox to unchecked or reconcile the execution state before resuming."
410: 		if task.Deferred {
411: 			expected = ExecuteTaskDeferred
412: 			problem = "plan deferral is not recorded in execution state"
413: 			detail = "top-level task uses [/] without a matching deferred run-state record"
414: 			suggestion = "Resume the owning execute attempt so it can record the deferral, or restore the task marker to unchecked."
415: 		}
416: 		if byID[task.ID] != expected {
417: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Tasks", task.Name, planPath, problem, detail, suggestion))
418: 		}
419: 	}
420: 	return findings
421: }

423: func (s Service) agentDeferredTaskReason(sp Sprint, taskID string) (string, error) {
424: 	data, err := s.store.ReadArtifact(sp, StagePlan)
425: 	if err != nil {
426: 		return "", err
427: 	}
428: 	inputs, err := s.store.ReadPlanningInputs(sp)
429: 	if err != nil {
430: 		return "", err
431: 	}
432: 	catalog, parseFindings := project.ParseProjectIndex(inputs.ProjectIndex)
433: 	if len(parseFindings) > 0 {
434: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("project-index.md has malformed catalog rows")
435: 	}
436: 	manifest, findings := s.planManifest(sp, inputs, catalog)
437: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
438: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan manifest is invalid")
439: 	}
440: 	tasks, findings := extractExecutePlanTasks(data, manifest, true)
441: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
442: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("plan changed to an invalid task state")
443: 	}
444: 	for _, task := range tasks {
445: 		if task.ID == taskID && task.Deferred {
446: 			return task.DeferReason, nil
447: 		}
448: 	}
449: 	return "", nil
450: }

519: func renderExecuteQueue(currentTaskID string, queue []ExecutePlanTask) string {

547: func executeQueueFromState(records []ExecuteTaskRecord, tasks []ExecutePlanTask, taskID string) []ExecutePlanTask {
548: 	queue := make([]ExecutePlanTask, 0, len(records))
549: 	for _, record := range records {
550: 		if taskID != "" && record.ID != taskID {
551: 			continue
552: 		}
553: 		if record.Status == ExecuteTaskComplete || record.Status == ExecuteTaskDeferred {

555: 		}
556: 		if task := taskByID(tasks, record.ID); task.ID != "" {
557: 			queue = append(queue, task)
558: 		}
559: 	}
560: 	return queue
561: }

620: func reconcileExecuteState(existing ExecuteRunState, planned []ExecuteTaskRecord, now time.Time) ExecuteRunState {
621: 	byID := map[string]ExecuteTaskRecord{}
622: 	for _, task := range existing.Tasks {
623: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskRunning {
624: 			task.Status = ExecuteTaskFailed
625: 			task.CompletedAt = &now
626: 			task.Diagnostics = append(task.Diagnostics, ExecuteDiagnostic{Code: "stale-running", Message: "recovered stale running task on resume", At: now})

184: func ValidateExecuteRunState(root string, s Sprint, state ExecuteRunState, path string) error {
185: 	if state.SchemaVersion == 0 {

187: 	}
188: 	if state.SchemaVersion != ExecuteRunStateSchemaVersion {
189: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: schemaVersion %d", ErrExecuteRunStateUnsupported, path, state.SchemaVersion)
190: 	}
191: 	if state.Project == "" || state.Sprint == "" || state.Target.Path == "" || state.Target.Source == "" || state.PlanPath == "" || state.PlanFingerprint == "" || state.CreatedAt.IsZero() || state.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
192: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing required top-level fields", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path)
193: 	}
194: 	if state.Project != s.Project {
195: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: project mismatch %q", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, state.Project)
196: 	}
197: 	if state.Sprint != s.Slug {
198: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: sprint mismatch %q", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, state.Sprint)
199: 	}
200: 	if !safeRelPath(state.PlanPath) {
201: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsafe planPath", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path)
202: 	}
203: 	if _, err := resolveSprintContained(root, s, state.PlanPath); err != nil {
204: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsafe planPath: %w", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, err)
205: 	}

207: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: unsafe planFingerprint", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path)
208: 	}
209: 	if len(state.Tasks) == 0 {
210: 		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: missing tasks", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path)
211: 	}
212: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
213: 	for i, task := range state.Tasks {
214: 		if task.ID == "" || task.Identity.Name == "" || task.CreatedAt.IsZero() || task.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
215: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %d missing required fields", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, i)
216: 		}
217: 		if seen[task.ID] {
218: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: duplicate task id %q", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID)
219: 		}
220: 		seen[task.ID] = true
221: 		if strings.ContainsAny(task.ID+task.Identity.Name, "\x00\r\n") {
222: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %d has unsafe identity", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, i)
223: 		}
224: 		if task.Identity.PlanLine < 1 {
225: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %q has invalid planLine", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID)
226: 		}
227: 		if !ValidExecuteTaskStatus(task.Status) {
228: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %q has unsupported status %q", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID, task.Status)
229: 		}
230: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskDeferred {
231: 			if task.CompletedAt == nil {
232: 				return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: deferred task %q has no completion time", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID)
233: 			}
234: 			hasReason := false
235: 			for _, diagnostic := range task.Diagnostics {
236: 				if diagnostic.Code == "deferred" && strings.TrimSpace(diagnostic.Message) != "" {
237: 					hasReason = true
238: 					break
239: 				}
240: 			}
241: 			if !hasReason {
242: 				return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: deferred task %q has no rationale", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID)
243: 			}
244: 		}
245: 		if task.Attempts < 0 {
246: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %q has invalid attempts", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID)
247: 		}
248: 		if task.Status == ExecuteTaskRunning && task.StartedAt == nil {
249: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: running task %q missing startedAt", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID)
250: 		}
251: 		if isTerminalExecuteStatus(task.Status) && task.CompletedAt == nil {
252: 			return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: terminal task %q missing completedAt", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID)
253: 		}
254: 		for j, diagnostic := range task.Diagnostics {
255: 			if diagnostic.Code == "" || diagnostic.Message == "" || diagnostic.At.IsZero() || strings.ContainsAny(diagnostic.Code+diagnostic.Message, "\x00\r\n") {
256: 				return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %q diagnostic %d invalid", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID, j)
257: 			}
258: 		}
259: 		for j, evidence := range task.Evidence {
260: 			if evidence.Kind == "" || evidence.Summary == "" || strings.ContainsAny(evidence.Kind+evidence.Summary, "\x00\r\n") {
261: 				return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %q evidence %d invalid", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID, j)
262: 			}
263: 			if evidence.Path != "" && !safeRelPath(evidence.Path) {
264: 				return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s: task %q evidence %d has unsafe path", ErrExecuteRunStateMalformed, path, task.ID, j)
265: 			}
266: 		}
267: 	}
268: 	return nil
269: }
270: 
271: func isTerminalExecuteStatus(status ExecuteTaskStatus) bool {
272: 	return status == ExecuteTaskComplete || status == ExecuteTaskDeferred || status == ExecuteTaskFailed || status == ExecuteTaskCancelled
273: }
274: 
275: func safeRelPath(path string) bool {
276: 	if path == "" || filepath.IsAbs(path) {
277: 		return false
278: 	}
279: 	clean := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(path)))
280: 	return clean != "." && !strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") && !strings.Contains(clean, "\x00")
281: }

part.text: Checking whether the per-task model annotation actually reaches the runtime request:

reasoning_details.text:
Interesting — `runtimeRequest` line 1166-1181: when metadata["stage"] maps to a valid PlanningStage, the stage runtime override REPLACES req.Provider/req.Model. For execute stage: `s.runtimeForStage(StageExecute)` — if planning.execute_model set, the request's Provider/Model get set from the override. But note `executeSelectionForTask` per-task model annotation: execute.go computes taskSelection and uses it ONLY for prompt text and session matching — does the actual runtime REQUEST carry the annotated model?? Look at execute.go lines 241-249:

```go
runtimeReq := s.runtimeRequest(composedPrompt, map[string]string{
    "project": ..., "stage": string(StageExecute), "task": task.ID, "model_source": taskSelection.Source, ...
})
runtimeReq.WorkDir = target.Path
```

`runtimeRequest` sets Provider/Model from `s.runtimeForStage(stage)` override (planning.execute_model) if present. If a task has an inline `<!-- model: other/model -->` annotation, `taskSelection.Model = "other/model"`, but runtimeReq.Provider/Model come from the STAGE override (execute_model), NOT the annotation! Unless... let me check: does execute.go override req.Provider/Model after calling runtimeRequest? I don't see it. Lines 241-245 only set WorkDir, SessionID/SessionAction.

Wait — also `s.runtimeConfig` is the base: `req := s.runtimeConfig` — runtimeConfig has default Provider/Model (models.primary/default). Then stage override replaces if configured.

So the per-task model annotation changes:
1. The prompt TEXT ("Model source: plan.md task annotation") — cosmetic.
2. The session-continuation matching (batchSessionModel comparisons).
3. Metadata model_source.

But NOT the actual model sent to the provider?! That would make `<!-- model: ... -->` annotations FUNCTIONALLY INERT except for breaking session reuse! Let me verify by checking whether anything else applies taskSelection to the request. Search for "Provider" / "Model" assignments in execute.go... From my full read of execute.go above: no assignment of runtimeReq.Provider or runtimeReq.Model anywhere in Execute(). The only model-related thing is taskSelection used in prompts/metadata/session-matching.

Hold on — check `splitProviderModel` usage at service.go:1172-1175: inside runtimeRequest, `if override, ok := s.runtimeForStage(stage); ok { if override.Model != "" { req.Provider, req.Model = splitProviderModel(override.Model) } }`. StageExecute's StageRuntime comes from WithStageRuntime(map) — sprintRuntimeService sets stage runtime models from config planning.execute_model etc.

So with an annotated task model "openai/gpt-x" vs configured execute_model "anthropic/claude-y":
- Prompt says "Model source: plan.md task annotation", target model gpt-x.
- Runtime request Model = claude-y (from stage override).
- batchSessionModel becomes "openai/gpt-x" for that turn; next task without annotation gets batch selection anthropic/claude-y → models mismatch → continueSession=false → fresh-fallback full prompt. So the annotation's ONLY real effect is forcing fresh sessions!

And the recorded Runtime summary claims Model=gpt-x while the actual run used claude-y — state lies about which model executed the task. That's an error-truth defect + broken feature. Let me verify there is genuinely no application of the task model to the request. Also check test `executeSelectionForTask` precedence test — it tests selection computation only, not request propagation. And TestPlanAndExecuteInjectCompleteTechnicalHandbook doesn't cover models.

Let me search the whole repo for where ExecutePlanTask.Model might influence requests.

"Never modify the target implementation or planning workspace" — adding a test file to the target repo modifies the working tree. The target repo already has a dirty file (skills.go modified by user). I should avoid touching the repo. Instead, I can write a small standalone test in /tmp that imports the internal package? Internal packages can't be imported outside the module.

Alternative: reason from source alone — it's airtight: execute.go lines 241-249 construct the request via s.runtimeRequest which sets req.Provider/req.Model only from stageRuntime override or leaves runtimeConfig defaults; nothing applies taskSelection.Model. I can also empirically confirm via a scratch Go test placed in a temp dir with a go.mod replace pointing at the target? Internal packages still blocked for external module. 

Option: create the test INSIDE the repo but in /tmp copy of the repo? Copying the whole repo to /tmp and adding a test there is allowed (not modifying the original). Let me do that for high-confidence defects — actually the evidence is already conclusive from reading. But the doctrine asks for verification where possible. A quick empirical check would strengthen. Let me first continue hunting; then decide on empirical verification for top findings.

Actually wait — let me double-check `s.runtimeConfig`: maybe production wiring sets runtimeConfig per-request model from... no, it's static config. And check WithStageRuntime usage in app wiring (sprintRuntimeService) to see what stage models get set — planning.execute_model → StageExecute override. So in default production config WITH planning.execute_model set, annotated tasks run on execute_model. Without any stage overrides, they run on models.primary/default. Either way, never the annotation.

Also check code_context_test.go:228 shows other stages DO set request.Provider/Model from their selections (code context sets rt.request.Provider == "vendor"). So the pattern exists elsewhere; execute just doesn't do it for annotations. Actually wait — for execute, service.go:1172 applies stage override to req. For code-context they set explicitly. Fine.

Now Finding 2 candidates to develop:

**Finding A: resume silently degrades to fresh state on load error (corrupt state destroyed)** — execute.go:177. Also legacy v0 unsupported → same path. Observable: operator runs --resume after crash-corrupted file; command re-executes ALL tasks including completed ones (agent work redone, cost doubled), prior corrupt file overwritten at line 180 save destroying evidence. Counter-evidence: validateResolvedResumeTasks catches the case only when plan markers are resolved ([x]/[/]). If agent checked off completed tasks in plan.md (which prompts don't require...). Hmm wait — actually what DOES happen with plan checkboxes on completion? Nothing instructs the agent to check them; but validateResolvedResumeTasks exists because agents sometimes do. In the common case markers stay unchecked → silent fresh rerun. Severity medium-high (cost/redo, audit destruction), confidence high (behavior certain from code).

But is it a DEFECT vs design ("fresh state wins")? The pack lists it descriptively under unknowns... no wait, §4 note says "a resume attempt with unchecked plan tasks but an unreadable/malformed .run-state.json passes prepareExecute ... and proceeds with fresh state, overwriting the prior file". It's descriptive. As reviewer I judge: silent data-destructive fallback on resume = misleading behavior; at minimum an observability/error-truth gap: no warning surfaced. I'll report it (severity medium, high confidence).

**Finding B: reconcile keeps stale Target header when target changed between runs** — state.Target stays old while WorkDir/publication use new target; durable record lies about where work happened; also PlanFingerprint stale (fingerprint captured fresh at line 176 but DISCARDED since reconcile returns existing header!). Wait — look carefully:

```go

if existing, loadErr := LoadExecuteRunState(s.root, sp); loadErr == nil && req.Resume {
    state = reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now)
}
```

reconcileExecuteState(existing, records, now) → returns existing (header intact: old Target, old fingerprint) with Tasks=planned-substituted. So yes: on ANY resume, the freshly computed fingerprint and CURRENT target are discarded in favor of the original run's values. If plan.md legitimately changed between runs (task edits — which produce new IDs for changed tasks), the recorded fingerprint no longer matches the actual plan being executed. The fingerprint's purpose: detect plan drift. After resume-with-edits, state.fingerprint describes the OLD plan forever. Any downstream consumer comparing fingerprint to current plan sees mismatch → could falsely flag tampering, or worse, consumers trusting it see stale data. Who consumes PlanFingerprint? Let me grep. If nothing consumes it besides validation charset, impact is limited to audit truth.

Target staleness has harder impact: publication Root uses CURRENT target; state records OLD. Audit trail wrong. Also `.run-state.json` gets published to git with wrong target claim.

Severity: low-medium (audit truth), confidence high.

Events delivered during StartRun synchronously? pruntime.Event stream typically emitted during run; StartRun blocking until completion implies events stop before return. But `state.UpdatedAt = task.UpdatedAt` — mutating shared struct without... all under mutex. Main goroutine reads sessionSaveErr under mutex. **Finding H: DeferExecuteTask allows deferring a `running` task owned by a LIVE execute process?** Mutation lease serializes: live execute holds mutation lock; defer waits/blocks. acquireMutationContext blocks until acquired (or fails?). If execute crashed leaving running, lock released by lease expiry. OK.

**Finding I: WriteExecuteSummary non-atomic** — requirement binds atomicity to .run-state.json; execute.md truncation window tiny; regenerated every run. Non-issue.

**Finding J: dry-run persists context pack cache** — side effect contradicts read-only preview intent asserted for PromptExecute; CLI --dry-run writes cache into sprint dir. Minor observability/purity nit. Probably intended lazily-cache-on-runtime-composition... but dry-run isn't runtime composition. Low value; maybe mention as non-issue.

**Finding K: `executionTurn > 1 → "fresh-fallback"` metadata even when this turn IS a continuation? No—continueSession checked first. Right order. Non-issue.

**Finding L: queue staleness in fresh-fallback prompts (deferred task still listed queued)** — renderExecuteQueue lists full executionQueue including tasks completed/deferred earlier THIS run (queue computed pre-loop). For fresh-fallback turns, the prompt claims "This agent session owns the complete ordered queue below. Execute only the current task..." listing already-resolved siblings as queued. Agent confusion risk (might redo them!). Trigger: multi-task run where turn 1 completes task1 but yields NO session id (noSessionExecutionRuntime-like adapters) → turn 2 fresh-fallback prompt lists task1+task2 as queued with task2 current. Prompt says execute only current task — mitigated. Minor. Skip or non-issue.

Wait, actually more important: does the CONTINUATION prompt (RenderExecuteContinuationPrompt) omit queue entirely — yes it says queue remains in force. Fine.

**Finding M: `allExecuteTasksResolved` publication when invoked via `--task` completing final task — publishes whole implementation repo possibly containing changes from tasks executed in EARLIER sessions — intended.

**Finding N: publishExecuteStage workspace paths use sp.Path join — resolveSprintContained not used; publisher containment-checks against root. sp.Path inside root. Fine.

**Finding O: `hasFailedExecuteTask` returns error BEFORE deleteCompletedSessions and publication — failed run leaves sessions/stores for recovery (comment says intentional: recent failed stores remain available). Good.

**Finding P: result.Message "execute complete" even when some tasks deferred — accurate enough ("complete" includes deferred resolution). CLI renders Result + per-task statuses. Fine.

**Finding Q — IMPORTANT, check `executeQueueFromState` vs in-loop skip for DEFERRED tasks**: queue excludes deferred; loop skips non pending/failed/cancelled — deferred skipped silently. Good.

**Finding R: Resume + TaskID + batchSessionID**: reusableExecuteSession(records, taskID, model) filters to the requested task's OWN record — whose status must be pending/failed/cancelled (else loop skips). A failed task's own Runtime.SessionID reused → continue the FAILED session. Continuing a failed session might carry poisoned context; design choice. Skip.

**Finding S: `batchSessionModel` initial value when NOT resuming**: selection.Model — irrelevant since ID empty. Fine.

**Finding T — subtle: resume gate compares `state.Target.Path` vs `target.Path` with filepath.Clean equality — but state.Target could have different Source (.workspace.json vs project-index.md) with same path — fine, path equality is what matters.

Now let me check locks.go and durable_operations quickly for anything execute-specific, plus verify.go's ExecuteComplete gating, and glance at gitpublish Publisher.Publish for All=true semantics + push-on-no-commit. Then examine execute_state_test.go coverage claims, and finally run the test suite to make sure baseline green (tests-first evidence).

Also I want to double-check Finding 1 by looking at how OTHER stages apply per-task models — e.g., review/coverage flows set req.Provider/Model directly? rg showed code_context_test expects request.Provider=="vendor" — meaning somewhere sets it. For execute, nothing. Solid.

One more candidate: **`executeModelSelection` treats override "--model ''"?** TrimSpace empty→skip. Fine.

And **model annotation regex charset `[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]+`** — provider/model with ':'? OpenRouter-style "openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha" fits (slashes ok). Fine.

Let me also verify **`validateResolvedResumeTasks` expected-status mapping ignores attempts/history**: [/] requires EXACTLY deferred; [x] exactly complete. A task both checked AND deferred marker?? parseTopLevelTaskLine: checked=[x] prefix; isDeferredTaskLine checks [/] prefix — mutually exclusive prefixes. OK.

Now, **what happens on resume when state.Tasks contains records for tasks whose IDs no longer exist in plan** — dropped silently (Finding B2, history loss). Combined into B.

reasoning_details.text:
Confirmed beyond doubt. `runReviewer` (review.go:916) explicitly applies the selection model to the wire request: `req.Model = strings.TrimPrefix(m.Model, req.Provider+"/")`. Code context does the same (code_context.go:293-294). **Execute never applies `taskSelection.Model` (or `--model` override) to `runtimeReq.Provider/Model`.** The execute request's model comes solely from stage override (planning.execute_model) or runtimeConfig defaults.

This is Finding 1 — HIGH severity correctness/observability defect:
- CLI contract: `--model <provider/model>` documented for execute; it changes prompts/metadata/state but NOT the executed model.
- Plan annotation feature `<!-- model: provider/model -->`: same inertness + breaks session continuity (batchSessionModel switches to annotated value; next task mismatch → fresh-fallback), so the annotation actively degrades efficiency while not doing its job.
- State records Runtime.Model = annotated/override model while actual run used config model → durable audit lie published to git.
- Prompt tells agent "Model source: plan.md task annotation" with a model that is not used.

Tests: only pure-function tests; no test asserts request propagation (fake confidence).

Now let me verify empirically in a /tmp copy of the repo by writing a test that runs Execute with an annotation and asserts request.Model. Copy repo (excluding .git? need module deps — vendor? check go.mod / GOFLAGS). Simpler: run existing test infra — create a new _test.go file in internal/sprint inside the COPY.

1. cp -r ultraplan-go /tmp/opencode/ultraplan-go-copy (exclude .git to be fast? go build needs nothing from .git).
2. Add test file TestExecuteAppliesAnnotatedModelToRuntimeRequest mirroring batchExecutionRuntime but recording req.Provider/req.Model; plan with annotation; service WithStageRuntime(StageExecute: "cfg/model") + runtimeConfig default; assert req.Model != annotated (expected FAIL proving defect) — actually assert what IS: show req.Model == cfg/model despite annotation.
3. Run `go test ./internal/sprint -run TestExecute...`.

part.text: All major hypotheses are now verified. Checking the reporting convention used by sibling jobs:

reasoning_details.text:
Confirmed both required test files are absent at the frozen commit, while requirements.md's contract table explicitly lists them as sprint-owned deliverables, and the sprint-23 review itself marked their absence a blocker (R-1). Some coverage later landed in `efficiency_improvements_test.go` and `execute_state_test.go`, but the required runner-level classification matrix (missing-evidence / runtime-failed / cancelled / diagnostic-only), resume reconciliation tests, and command-level exit-code mapping remain absent — consistent with my independent analysis.

Now let me consolidate and do final counter-evidence sweeps on my finding list:

**F1 (High): per-task model annotation AND --model override never reach the runtime request.**
- Evidence: execute.go:241-249 (no Provider/Model assignment); service.go:1166-1181 (stage override only); contrast code_context.go:293-294 and review.go:916 which DO apply selections.
- Empirically reproduced 3 ways: wire stays "test/model" with annotation; wire stays "test/model" with --model override; annotated task forces fresh-fallback.
- Bad outcomes: tasks execute on wrong model while state/prompt claim otherwise (audit lie published to git via .run-state.json); documented CLI flag inert; annotations actively break session reuse → cost blowup.
- Counter-evidence searched: no other assignment path; runtimeRequest only applies stage overrides; WithStageRuntime wiring is static config. Tests only cover pure selection function (execute_plan_test.go:197-202) — fake confidence.
- Severity: High (wrong-model execution + audit corruption + broken contract). Confidence: High.

**F2 (Medium-High): `--resume` silently degrades to full fresh re-execution on any run-state load error, destroying the prior artifact.**
- Evidence: execute.go:177-182. loadErr ignored for ALL error classes (missing/malformed/unsupported/DB failure). First Save overwrites file.
- Empirically reproduced: truncated JSON → resume re-ran completed task (calls=2), replaced file, exit 0, message "execute complete", attempts reset to 1 (history erased).
- Partial control: validateResolvedResumeTasks catches it ONLY when plan has [x]/[/] markers matching; prompts never instruct checking [x], so common case slips through.
- Bad outcome: silent duplicate agent execution of completed work (cost, double-applied changes), forensic evidence destroyed, operator told "execute complete" with no hint.
- Severity: Medium-High. Confidence: High.

**F3 (Medium): stale-running reconcile on resume keeps stale header: Target.Path and PlanFingerprint frozen from first run even when target/plan changed.**
- Evidence: execute.go:176-179 (fresh fingerprint/target computed then discarded by reconcile), reconcileExecuteState:620-638 keeps existing header.
- Empirically reproduced: after repointing project-index to a copy-target and resuming successfully, persisted Target.Path still = old dir while WorkDir/publication root = new dir; fingerprint unchanged despite plan re-read.
- Bad outcome: published `.run-state.json` misattributes where implementation work happened and which plan version was executed; auditors/status consumers misled; wholesale commit root differs from recorded approved target.
- Note nuance: target change usually fails closed at context-pack validation unless new tree matches references — narrow but real window (repo moved/copied, or context refs satisfied).
- Severity: Medium (error truth/audit), Confidence: High (behavior proven).

**F4 (Medium): data race window between late OnEvent delivery and post-run state mutation.**
- Evidence: platform/runtime/runtime.go:400 (`time.After(time.Second)` drain cap then return while events goroutine continues calling req.OnEvent); execute.go:253-268 OnEvent mutates task.Runtime/state under sessionMu, but main-loop writes at execute.go:275,283-284 and subsequent SaveExecuteRunState calls are unsynchronized against that goroutine; saveExecuteRunStateWithHooks also mutates state.UpdatedAt.
- Bad outcome: -race-detectable memory race; potential lost-update where a straggler checkpoint save (older snapshot) overwrites a newer terminal save (both atomic renames, last-writer-wins) → e.g., next task's running transition reverted in file.
- Trigger: events channel not drained within 1s of Wait returning (large event streams/slow disk).
- Counter-evidence: if agentwrap guarantees Events() closed before Wait returns... the explicit 1s timeout proves non-drain is considered possible; no ordering guarantee documented in Request.OnEvent contract.
- Severity: Medium. Confidence: Medium (mechanism certain; practical frequency uncertain; depends on external adapter timing).

**F5 (Medium): documented safe-diagnostic completion route unreachable + untested.**
- Evidence: execute.go:307-309 + 671-678 require warning containing "diagnostic-only"; in-repo producers of Result.Warnings: runtime.go:398 (dropped-events text), runtime_metrics.go:122 (metrics text) — neither matches; pinned agentwrap emits only "OpenCode finished without..." warnings and pass-through warn-type native events (no diagnostic-only producer); zero tests exercise the branch; cli-reference.md documents "requires runtime evidence or a safe diagnostic"; RenderExecutePrompt instructs agents accordingly; sprint-23 plan/requirements require tests for this path (never written).
- Bad outcome: agent produces explicit safe diagnostic explaining why machine-verifiable evidence is impossible → run still classified failed/missing-evidence; queue halts; operator must manually defer. Contract promises otherwise. Alternatively if OpenCode does emit such warnings, an untested trust-gated classification drives completion with zero evidence — either way the gate is not verified.
- Severity: Medium. Confidence: Medium-High for "unreachable from assembled in-repo system"; framed carefully.

**F6 (Low-Medium): exit-code classification by substring; checkpoint-save errors misclassified as ExitRuntime.**
- Evidence: sprint_commands.go:360-365; execute.go:318 message contains "runtime". No tests for execute exit codes (only QA table). 
- Bad outcome: automation distinguishing partial-failure vs runtime vs persistence gets wrong class; e.g., local disk-full during checkpoint reports as runtime-class.
- Severity: Low-Medium. Confidence: High.

**F7 (verification gap, cross-cutting): required test files from sprint-23 contract absent; resume machinery production-exercised via flow (Resume:true always) with zero direct tests.**
- Evidence: ls shows files missing; requirements.md contract table lists both; sprint-23 review R-1 blocker quote; flow.go:241 Resume:true; rg confirms no sprint-package test constructs Resume:true.
- This overlaps F1-F5 evidence; report as its own finding under verification lens.

Non-issues / defended:
- Containment-by-assignment WorkDir=target.Path: contained by construction within this surface; ValidateExecuteWorkdir unused dead code (minor cleanup note, not a defect since nothing else sets WorkDir — runtimeRequest sets s.root but Execute always overwrites before StartRun).
- All=true publication sweeping whole worktree: documented design.
- gitpublish CAS/push semantics: sound; commit-skip when tree unchanged prevents redundant pushes.
- DB-mirror checkpoint semantics: coherent (file mirrors once terminal; Load prefers DB).
- Defer protocol layers: consistent rationale enforcement end-to-end.
- Stop-on-failure & persist-before-launch: tested and correct.
- WriteExecuteSummary non-atomicity: acceptable; requirement binds atomicity to .run-state.json.
- Dry-run persisting context-pack cache: minor inconsistency with PromptExecute read-only preview; disposable cache; not reported as defect (mention briefly).

One more check on F4 counter-evidence: does execute's own test TestExecuteFailsAndRecordsFailedTaskWhenSessionCheckpointCannotBePersisted fire OnEvent synchronously? Yes — fake runtime calls req.OnEvent inline before returning; real adapter may deliver async up to 1s+ after return. Also check whether Adapter.StartRun could return while eventsCh send is pending — yes line 400.

Also confirm exact line numbers for citations in final report:
- execute.go:177 (load ignore), :180 save, :186-193 reuse gate, :216 running persist, :245 WorkDir, :253-268 OnEvent wrapper, :275 mergeRuntimeSummary write, :283-284 UpdatedAt writes, :286-313 classification switch, :307-309 diag-only, :310-312 missing-evidence, :317-319 checkpoint error return, :338-340 delete sessions, :341-347 publish.
- service.go:1122-1195 runtimeRequest; 1166-1181 stage override; 1174 assignment.
- review.go:914-916 contrast; code_context.go:293-294 contrast.
- runtime.go:400 1s drain.
- sprint_commands.go:356-366 classification; parseSprintExecuteArgs 1277-1317.
- reconcileExecuteState 620-638.
- validateResolvedResumeTasks 386-421.
- reusableExecuteSession 563-574.
- flow.go:240-242 Resume:true.

For F1 severity justification: also note metadata model_source records "plan.md task annotation"/"command override" — published state claims wrong model. And prompt tells agent its model.

Also double-check F1's --model claim once more: is there maybe handling in operation_runner/web paths? They call same Execute. And CLI builds execService = sprintRuntimeService(...) — static config. Confirmed.

Wait, one more possible mitigations for F2 I should verify: does prepareExecute→validateResolvedResumeTasks get bypassed because extraction with allowChecked=true returns Checked tasks and my probe had NO checked markers (agent didn't check them)? Right — validPlan task stays unchecked since batchExecutionRuntime doesn't edit plan.md. In production, agents following RenderExecutePrompt are NOT instructed to check [x] on completion (only [/] deferral instructions exist) — so completed markers being unchecked is the EXPECTED steady state, making F2's trigger the norm, not edge. Good.

Also confirm attempts reset observed: probe printed "attempts now=1" — old record had Attempts=1 from run 1; after redo it's again 1 (fresh record), losing cumulative attempt history. Included.

Now — the job says "Return substantive findings and defended/non-issues only". Where to write? The instruction says work independently, return findings. Previous jobs wrote result.md artifacts. I'll write a findings report to review/jobs/? The task says "Review artifacts: .../review" and "Return substantive findings and defended/non-issues only". As the reviewer I should produce the report. Let me check how other job results are structured to match convention (e.g., look at an existing attempt/result file from another surface job).
